findings.first_evidence: scripts/e2e/cleanup.mjs:47-48 `if (!environment.split('\0').includes(`ONTOKIT_E2E_RUN=${manifest.id}`) || !command.split('\0').includes(fileURLToPath(new URL('./supervisor.mjs', import.meta.url)))) throw new Error('Host process is not a run supervisor; refusing cleanup');` / `if (!sameProcess(record, current)) throw new Error('Process identity changed; refusing cleanup');`
findings.suggested_fix: Check the recorded boot/start/group identity before reading or signaling its current PID. Skip only a proven obsolete identity, never signal its replacement, then clean verified marked descendants and independently label-checked Docker/runtime resources. Preserve refusal for ambiguous ownership or surviving owned processes. Add a regression that preserves an unrelated replacement process while completing owned cleanup.
findings.title: Recycled supervisor PID prevents explicit crash cleanup
findings.why_it_matters: After a hard interruption, a recorded supervisor PID can be reused by an unrelated process. cleanupProcesses then throws before Docker and private runtime removal, so the documented recovery command cannot reclaim owned resources while that unrelated process remains alive. The process must remain unsignalled, but an obsolete identity need not prevent cleanup of independently verified owned resources.
findings.validation_reason: The new cleanup.mjs:40-48 throws when a same-boot recorded supervisor PID has been recycled, and cleanup.mjs:61 consequently prevents both marked-descendant cleanup and independently label-verified Docker/runtime cleanup; runtime.mjs:76-79 persists supervisor identities, so killing the launcher and supervisors before recovery makes this precondition reachable, while refusing to signal the unrelated process does not require abandoning separately verified resources (incidence was not measured).

findings.title: Incomplete retained diagnostics block subsequent harness launches
findings.why_it_matters: A hard interruption after creating a retention directory but before writing metadata.json leaves an entry that expireDiagnostics rejects on every subsequent launch. This occurs before a run manifest or phase is created; the CLI suppresses the actual error, leaving users unable to start another suite or identify the blocking directory.
findings.validation_reason: The new diagnostics.mjs:35-40 publishes the retention directory before metadata.json, so a hard interruption in that interval leaves an own-created entry whose missing metadata throws at diagnostics.mjs:15 on every subsequent run.mjs:24 startup, before phase/manifest creation, and run.mjs:125-126 hides its cause; the exception cleanup at diagnostics.mjs:41-45 cannot run after SIGKILL, establishing the trigger without relying on malformed or foreign metadata (incidence was not measured).

triage_groups.title: Recovery after hard interruption
triage_groups.context: A stale process record or incomplete diagnostics entry can stop later recovery or startup.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix each ownership-preserving recovery path and add its targeted regression before rerunning lifecycle verification.
triage_groups.why: Both are interruption edge cases in the disposable harness, with independent fixes.

requirements.requirement: R1. A documented local invocation provisions fresh real services and test identities without adopting, modifying or deleting another run's or developer's resources.
requirements.evidence: e2e/README.md; e2e/compose.yaml; scripts/e2e/ownership.mjs; bootstrap-identity.mjs. Fresh source/storage/identity isolation and unchanged neighboring resource identities are recorded in the supplied receipts.

requirements.requirement: R2. The suite hard-fails unmet prerequisites and bounded readiness failures; a missing backend or skipped full-stack test cannot count as success.
requirements.evidence: scripts/e2e/run.mjs; full-stack.mjs; evidence.mjs and evidence.test.mjs. Prerequisites/readiness fail closed; all 21 mandatory tests must pass with no skips, retries, flaky outcomes or runner errors.

requirements.requirement: R3. Genuine OIDC authentication supplies the browser session and API credentials used by the tests, without synthetic session injection or a production authentication bypass.
requirements.evidence: scripts/e2e/bootstrap-identity.mjs; e2e/stack.setup.ts; fixtures/auth.ts; auth-foundation.spec.ts. Genuine OIDC owner/unrelated sessions supply credentials, with a fresh UI session in the Chromium journey.

requirements.requirement: R4. API tests prove project creation, reading, updating and deletion, plus ontology import, class/property reads and persisted source changes.
requirements.evidence: e2e/api/projects.spec.ts and ontology.spec.ts cover CRUD, import, branch initialization, class/property labels and immutable persisted source revisions.

requirements.requirement: R5. API tests prove branch creation, revision-aware source saving, pull-request diff and merge, and persisted target-branch content.
requirements.evidence: e2e/api/branches.spec.ts and pull-requests.spec.ts cover branch isolation, stale revision rejection, diff review, ordinary-owner merge and persisted target content.

requirements.requirement: R6. API tests prove project-local lexical search and worker-backed lint completion against the imported ontology.
requirements.evidence: e2e/api/search-lint.spec.ts checks exact lexical search results and fresh, completed, persisted worker lint runs under bounded polling.

requirements.requirement: R7. API tests prove unauthorized, forbidden, absent-resource and invalid-input contracts, including absence of unintended mutation after a rejected write.
requirements.evidence: e2e/api/errors.spec.ts checks 401/403/404/422, malformed imports and independent no-mutation assertions after rejected writes.

requirements.requirement: R8. A Chromium test performs real login, ontology import, editor navigation, branch editing, saving, pull-request review and merge, then verifies the result after reloading.
requirements.evidence: e2e/browser/ontology-workflow.spec.ts drives fresh login, UI import, navigation, branch edit/save, PR review/merge and target reload assertions; mandatory fresh-run evidence is supplied.

requirements.requirement: R9. Success, setup failure, test failure and catchable interruption remove all run-owned resources and credentials; hard interruption leaves a narrowly scoped recovery record for explicit cleanup.
requirements.evidence: scripts/e2e/cleanup.mjs; ownership.mjs; supervisor.mjs; docs/releases/d06-lifecycle-readiness.md and d06-u6-verification.json address every lifecycle path and explicit recovery. Recovery implementation has the bounded defects #1/#2; this is implementation coverage, not unconditional acceptance.

requirements.requirement: R10. Completion evidence maps every B10 obligation to tests and results while retaining B11–B13 and live DEV acceptance as separate unfinished requirements.
requirements.evidence: docs/releases/d06-full-stack-readiness.md, d06-u6-verification.json, durable run receipts and the requirements roadmap map B10 to tests and retain B11-B13/live DEV as unfinished.
